A Redis-backed implementation of `CacheServiceAbs` that stores and retrieves JSON-serialized values using Spring's `RedisTemplate`, with colon-delimited key namespacing and a companion expiration-tracking key per entry.

## Key Components

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `RedisCacheService` | Spring `@Service("redisCache")` bean extending `CacheServiceAbs` |
| `valueOps` | `ValueOperations` handle for Redis string operations |
| `EXPIRATION_SUFFIX` | Constant `":expiration"` appended to keys that track insert timestamps |
| `buildRedisKey(cachePath, key)` | Constructs the full Redis key as `cachePath:key` |
| `get(...)` | Retrieves and deserializes a cached value; auto-invalidates on deserialization failure |
| `put(cachePath, key, value)` | Serializes and stores a value alongside its `Expiration` timestamp entry |
| `invalidate(cachePath, key)` | Deletes both the primary key and its companion expiration key |
| `getInsertTime(cachePath, key)` | Reads the companion expiration key to return the original insert timestamp |

## Usage Example

```java
// Inject the named bean
@Qualifier("redisCache")
@Autowired
private RedisCacheService cacheService;

// Store a value
cacheService.put("github", "user:octocat", someUserObject);

// Retrieve with a 10-minute refresh interval (600_000 ms)
Optional<GithubUser> cached = cacheService.get(
    "github",
    "user:octocat",
    new TypeToken<GithubUser>() {},
    600_000L
);

// Resulting Redis keys:
// "github:user:octocat"            → JSON payload
// "github:user:octocat:expiration" → {"timestamp": 1718000000000}

// Invalidate both keys
cacheService.invalidate("github", "user:octocat");
```
